sources.label: DORA (Level 1)
sources.intervalBecause: Arts. 2 and 16 read in full against the EUR-Lex text on 2026-08-09 to settle which entities are excluded from inside the financial-entity list, and to establish that Art. 16 disapplies Arts. 5 to 15 only and does NOT reach the Chapter III reporting obligation. Three shipped receipts now carry that reading, and the wrong one - Art. 16 as an exemption from reporting - is a single plausible edit away. A change here makes a customer-facing receipt wrong rather than merely stale.

sources.label: DORA incident-reporting RTS
sources.version: OJ 20.2.2025; made under DORA Art. 19(4) VERSIONED 2026-08-11 (BL-46): all four Art. 5 windows confirmed VERBATIM against the OJ text - 5(1)(a) four hours from classification and 24 from awareness, 5(2) the late-classification carve-out, 5(1)(b) 72 hours, 5(1)(c) one month. ⚠️ TWO CORRECTIONS: the empowerment for the TIME LIMITS is Article 20, third subparagraph (the RTS's own citation line), not Article 19(4) which is the reporting obligation - both are relevant and they do different jobs, and the 19(4) label rests on the RTS's in-text cross-reference rather than a direct read, because EUR-Lex truncates DORA Arts. 19/20. And Article 5 has SIX paragraphs, not five: 5(6) lets a competent authority disapply the 5(4) relief for an entity that is significant or has a systemic character. It changes no computed number - the engine never applies 5(4) - but the Limits section was incomplete.

sources.label: SEC Item 106 of Regulation S-K
sources.instrument: 17 C.F.R. s 229.106; Form 8-K Item 1.05, prescribed at 17 CFR 249.308, General Instruction B.1 (the four-business-day window and the day-zero convention) and General Instruction 2 (the amendment window)
sources.version: adopted text at 88 FR 51942 and 51945 - ⚠️ THOSE TWO PINCITES ARE UNVERIFIED and are deliberately left marked. The Federal Register release PDF this project can open truncates before the amendatory text, so the page numbers could not be confirmed against the pages themselves. What IS corroborated: 88 FR 51896, 4 Aug. 2023, effective 5 Sep. 2023. Do not quietly drop the marker to tidy the row - an unmarked pincite reads as checked. VERSIONED 2026-08-11 (BL-46): the four-business-day window comes from FORM 8-K, GENERAL INSTRUCTION B.1 (the Form is prescribed at 17 CFR 249.308) - NOT s 229.105 (Risk Factors), NOT s 229.106 (the annual item), and not the body of Item 1.05. The same Instruction also supplies the day-zero convention this engine implements: where the event falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday the period 'shall begin to run on, and include, the first business day thereafter'. Instruction 2 sets a SECOND four-business-day amendment clock, which this engine does not compute and states as a deviation.

sources.version: pending; no Commission action recorded as at 2026-08-09. A petition is not a proposal and not a rule — this row exists because the product now names it, and a claim about pendency decays the moment the Commission acts
sources.intervalBecause: the claim carried in the product is that the Commission HAS NOT ACTED. That is a negative about a live docket, and the day it stops being true every sentence citing it becomes wrong. 365 days is a year of being wrong; the disclosure-clock rows moved to 180 for the weaker version of the same argument

citationAllowlist.reason: Named ONLY to say it is the WRONG locus for the four-business-day window, in the comment that versions the constant (BL-46). Regulation S-K s 229.105 is Risk Factors; the window comes from Form 8-K General Instruction B.1, which the row for sec-item-106 declares. This engine relies on nothing s 229.105 says. Naming the wrong section is the point of the sentence - somebody previously cited it, and 'not this one' is only useful if it says which one - so the number stays and this allowlist carries the argument rather than the citation check being loosened. Permanent, not pending.
